name: H.E. Hakainde Hichilema
role: President of the Republic of Zambia

scoreBreakdown.explanation: President Hichilema has demonstrated strong leadership in restructuring Zambia's unsustainable debt through a historic IMF Extended Credit Facility and successful Eurobond restructuring. His administration introduced key governance reforms including the reconstitution of the Constitutional Court and strengthened the independence of the Anti-Corruption Commission.
positiveFactors: Successfully negotiated Zambia's $6.3 billion external debt restructuring under the G20 Common Framework
Reconstituted the Constitutional Court and strengthened judicial independence
Maintained Cabinet discipline with clear performance benchmarks for ministers
Appointed technocrats to key economic positions, improving policy credibility
negativeFactors: Perceived slow pace of decentralization reforms despite campaign promises
Some provincial appointments criticized for regional imbalance
improvementTips: Accelerate the decentralization agenda by devolving more fiscal authority to provincial administrations
Ensure regional balance in senior government appointments to strengthen national cohesion
Establish a formal mid-term governance review mechanism with public reporting

scoreBreakdown.explanation: The administration has delivered meaningful policy outcomes in free education, CDF fund increases, and the recruitment of over 30,000 teachers and health workers. However, the cost of living remains high for many Zambians, and the mining sector fiscal regime reforms have been slower than anticipated.
positiveFactors: Introduced free education from Early Childhood Education through Grade 12, increasing enrollment by 18%
Increased Constituency Development Fund allocation from K1.6 million to K28.3 million per constituency
Recruited over 30,000 teachers and 11,000 health workers to address critical public sector vacancies
Launched the Comprehensive Agriculture Support Programme benefiting 1 million smallholder farmers
negativeFactors: Inflation remains above 10%, eroding household purchasing power despite fiscal consolidation efforts
Mining sector fiscal reforms delayed, limiting revenue diversification from copper and gold exports
improvementTips: Fast-track mining fiscal regime reforms to capture greater value from rising copper prices
Implement targeted social cash transfer expansions to cushion vulnerable households from inflation
Develop a comprehensive industrial policy to promote value addition in the mining and agriculture sectors

scoreBreakdown.explanation: President Hichilema maintains solid public support, particularly in Southern, Western, and North-Western provinces. His personal integrity and anti-corruption stance resonate with citizens. However, expectations remain high, and some urban voters express frustration with the pace of economic improvement and job creation.
positiveFactors: Afrobarometer survey indicates 65% trust rating, above the African average of 48%
Strong personal brand as a self-made businessman with perceived financial integrity
Regular public engagement through social media and provincial tours
Zambia's improved international credit outlook has boosted national confidence
negativeFactors: Youth unemployment remains above 25%, generating frustration among young urban voters
Some rural communities feel disconnected from Lusaka-centered policy discussions
Media freedom concerns raised by press organizations regarding selected incidents
improvementTips: Launch a dedicated national youth employment and entrepreneurship programme with measurable annual targets
Increase presidential visits and town halls in rural districts beyond provincial capitals
Strengthen engagement with media organizations and recommit to press freedom protections publicly

scoreBreakdown.explanation: President Hichilema is widely regarded as one of Zambia's most ethical leaders, with a strong anti-corruption track record. His administration has pursued corruption cases from prior regimes and maintained a relatively clean Cabinet. The Financial Intelligence Centre has been empowered to operate more independently under his tenure.
positiveFactors: No personal corruption allegations or unexplained wealth controversies during tenure
Empowered the Anti-Corruption Commission and Drug Enforcement Commission to pursue high-profile cases
Declared personal assets publicly, setting a transparency benchmark for future leaders
Cabinet ministers required to declare assets and subjected to lifestyle audits
negativeFactors: Critics allege selective prosecution of corruption cases targeting primarily opposition-linked individuals
Some UPND party officials at local level implicated in tender irregularities without swift action
improvementTips: Ensure anti-corruption enforcement is visibly non-partisan by pursuing all credible cases regardless of political affiliation
Establish a zero-tolerance disciplinary framework for ruling party officials involved in procurement irregularities
Publish an annual presidential integrity report documenting anti-corruption milestones and ongoing investigations

scoreBreakdown.explanation: Zambia's international standing has improved significantly under President Hichilema, with restored credibility among multilateral institutions and strengthened bilateral ties. The successful debt restructuring restored Zambia's reputation in global capital markets. Zambia has taken a more active role in SADC and AU diplomacy.
positiveFactors: Restored Zambia's credibility with the IMF, World Bank, and international capital markets through fiscal discipline
Attracted significant foreign direct investment commitments in mining, energy, and agriculture
Strengthened Zambia-US relations with a presidential visit to Washington and expanded AGOA trade benefits
Played a constructive mediation role in regional SADC political disputes
negativeFactors: Relations with China perceived as cooling, potentially affecting infrastructure financing pipeline
Limited progress on diversifying diplomatic engagement beyond traditional Western and Chinese partners
improvementTips: Develop a comprehensive multi-vector foreign policy that balances Western, Chinese, and South-South partnerships
Strengthen economic diplomacy capacity in Zambian embassies to attract investment from Gulf states and India
Take a more visible leadership role in African Union climate change and energy transition negotiations

overallExplanation: President Hakainde Hichilema has delivered a credible governance performance anchored in fiscal discipline, anti-corruption commitment, and restored international credibility. The landmark debt restructuring and expanded social spending on education and healthcare represent significant policy achievements. However, persistent inflation, high youth unemployment, and the need for faster mining sector reforms temper the overall assessment. His strong ethical standing and institutional reforms position Zambia well for continued progress if economic policy delivery accelerates in the second half of his term.
topImprovementAreas: Accelerate mining fiscal reforms and industrial policy to diversify the economy and create jobs
Address youth unemployment with a dedicated national programme targeting measurable outcomes
Strengthen rural engagement and ensure anti-corruption enforcement is visibly non-partisan

name: Edgar Chagwa Lungu
role: Former President of the Republic of Zambia

scoreBreakdown.explanation: President Lungu's leadership was marked by a centralization of power and the controversial Bill 10 constitutional amendment attempt. While he maintained political stability and managed the initial COVID-19 response, governance institutions were weakened through political interference, and the independence of the judiciary and anti-corruption bodies was compromised during his tenure.
positiveFactors: Maintained national stability during a period of regional political turbulence
Oversaw the initial COVID-19 pandemic response including lockdown coordination and vaccine procurement
Expanded road infrastructure through the Link Zambia 8000 programme
negativeFactors: Bill 10 constitutional amendment widely criticized as an attempt to concentrate executive power
Perceived political interference in the judiciary and the Anti-Corruption Commission
Cabinet reshuffles were frequent and often politically motivated rather than performance-based
Public Order Act used to restrict opposition political activities and civic space
improvementTips: Future leaders should protect the independence of governance institutions from executive interference
Constitutional amendment processes should involve genuine broad-based national consultation
Cabinet stability and merit-based appointments are essential for effective governance delivery

scoreBreakdown.explanation: The Lungu administration invested heavily in infrastructure, particularly roads, hospitals, and universities. However, these investments were largely debt-financed, contributing to Zambia's default on its Eurobond obligations in 2020. Social sector spending was squeezed by debt servicing, and key policy reforms in agriculture and mining were not advanced.
positiveFactors: Constructed multiple road projects under Link Zambia 8000 connecting rural areas to economic centres
Built and upgraded hospitals including Levy Mwanawasa University Teaching Hospital expansion
Established new public universities including Mukuba and Chalimbana
Expanded social cash transfer coverage to additional vulnerable households
negativeFactors: Zambia became the first African country to default on sovereign debt during COVID-19 in November 2020
External debt ballooned from $6 billion to over $14 billion during his tenure
Power deficit crisis (load shedding) worsened due to inadequate investment in energy diversification
Agricultural subsidies through FISP were poorly targeted with significant leakage to non-eligible beneficiaries
improvementTips: Infrastructure investment must be balanced with fiscal sustainability and transparent debt management
Agricultural subsidy programmes require robust targeting mechanisms and regular audits to prevent leakage
Energy policy must prioritize diversification beyond hydropower to prevent recurring load shedding crises

scoreBreakdown.explanation: President Lungu initially enjoyed strong public support following his 2015 by-election victory, but trust eroded significantly over his tenure due to rising cost of living, perceived corruption, and restrictions on civic freedoms. His narrow 2016 re-election victory reflected a deeply divided electorate, and his approval rating dropped below 40% by the end of his second term.
positiveFactors: Maintained a loyal base of support particularly in Lusaka, Eastern, and Muchinga provinces
Personally approachable and connected with ordinary citizens through informal engagements
Responded to public pressure on some issues such as fuel subsidy adjustments
negativeFactors: Approval rating declined from approximately 55% in 2016 to below 40% by 2021
Widespread public perception of corruption within the administration despite limited prosecutions
Closure of The Post newspaper and harassment of independent media eroded public trust in governance
Cost of living increases, particularly mealie meal and fuel prices, fuelled public discontent
improvementTips: Leaders must protect media freedom as a cornerstone of public trust and democratic accountability
Transparent communication about economic challenges and policy trade-offs builds and maintains public confidence
Addressing cost of living concerns through targeted interventions is critical to sustaining popular support

scoreBreakdown.explanation: The Lungu administration faced persistent corruption allegations involving senior government officials and politically connected individuals. While President Lungu himself was not formally charged during his tenure, several close associates were implicated in procurement irregularities and illicit enrichment. The weakening of anti-corruption institutions during his watch contributed to a culture of impunity.
positiveFactors: No personal criminal convictions or formal charges against President Lungu during his tenure
Established the Financial Intelligence Centre to monitor suspicious financial transactions
negativeFactors: Multiple Cabinet ministers and senior officials faced corruption allegations without consequence during his tenure
Procurement of firefighting equipment, ambulances, and road construction contracts marred by cost inflation scandals
The Anti-Corruption Commission was perceived as politically compromised and unable to pursue cases against ruling party officials
Unexplained wealth accumulation by several officials close to the presidency raised public concern
improvementTips: Anti-corruption agencies must be constitutionally protected from political interference to function effectively
Public procurement oversight should include independent civil society monitoring and real-time disclosure
Asset declaration requirements for all senior officials must be enforced with meaningful penalties for non-compliance

scoreBreakdown.explanation: Zambia maintained functional international relationships during the Lungu era, with particularly strong ties to China through Belt and Road Initiative infrastructure projects. However, relations with Western nations and multilateral institutions became strained over democratic governance concerns and the growing debt burden. Zambia's debt default in 2020 severely damaged its international financial reputation.
positiveFactors: Secured significant Chinese investment in infrastructure through the Belt and Road Initiative
Maintained Zambia's tradition of regional peace and stability, hosting refugees from neighbouring countries
Continued diplomatic engagement across SADC and the African Union
Attracted investment in the Lusaka South Multi-Facility Economic Zone
negativeFactors: Zambia's sovereign debt default in 2020 damaged international financial credibility
Growing concern from Western governments about democratic backsliding and civic space restrictions
Over-reliance on Chinese debt financing raised sovereignty concerns domestically and internationally
Reduced access to concessional financing from multilateral development banks due to debt levels
improvementTips: Diversified international partnerships reduce dependence on any single creditor or trading partner
Maintaining democratic standards and civil liberties is essential for productive Western diplomatic engagement
Sovereign debt management must be transparent and sustainable to preserve international credibility

overallExplanation: Edgar Lungu's presidency delivered visible infrastructure development but at an unsustainable fiscal cost that culminated in Zambia's historic sovereign debt default in 2020. His tenure was characterized by a tension between developmental ambition and governance weaknesses, including democratic backsliding, corruption allegations against senior officials, and the erosion of institutional independence. While he maintained political stability and expanded physical infrastructure, the accumulation of unsustainable debt, restrictions on civic space, and failure to advance key structural reforms significantly diminish his overall governance legacy.
topImprovementAreas: Fiscal discipline and transparent debt management must accompany any infrastructure investment programme
Anti-corruption institutions require constitutional protection from political interference
Media freedom and civic space protections are non-negotiable pillars of democratic governance

name: Michael Chilufya Sata
role: Former President of the Republic of Zambia

scoreBreakdown.explanation: President Sata brought a decisive and action-oriented leadership style that resonated with Zambians weary of perceived bureaucratic inertia. Known as 'King Cobra' for his sharp political instincts, he drove rapid infrastructure development in Lusaka and demonstrated a hands-on approach to governance. However, his leadership was also marked by authoritarian tendencies, frequent Cabinet reshuffles, and a concentration of decision-making in the presidency.
positiveFactors: Decisive leadership style that accelerated infrastructure development, particularly in Lusaka's road network
Created new provinces (Muchinga) and districts to improve administrative coverage of remote areas
Personally inspected government projects, holding officials directly accountable for delivery
Raised the minimum wage significantly, improving conditions for low-income workers
negativeFactors: Frequent and unpredictable Cabinet reshuffles created governance instability
Centralized decision-making in the presidency reduced institutional effectiveness of line ministries
Health challenges during the last year of his presidency created a power vacuum and governance uncertainty
improvementTips: Cabinet stability and continuity are essential for sustained policy implementation
Presidential succession planning and health transparency protocols should be institutionalized
Delegating authority to ministers with clear mandates improves governance efficiency

scoreBreakdown.explanation: The Sata administration delivered visible and rapid infrastructure improvements, particularly in Lusaka's road network and urban housing. His pro-poor policies including minimum wage increases and increased social spending were popular. However, policy implementation was often ad hoc, and the administration lacked a coherent long-term economic strategy beyond infrastructure expansion.
positiveFactors: Transformed Lusaka's road network with major dual carriageway construction projects
Raised the national minimum wage from K419 to K700 per month, benefiting millions of workers
Launched the Patriotic Front's pro-poor agenda with increased social sector budget allocations
Started construction of the Kazungula Bridge connecting Zambia to Botswana for regional trade
negativeFactors: Economic management lacked a comprehensive medium-term strategy, with policy decisions often reactive
Agricultural sector received insufficient attention compared to urban infrastructure
Mining tax regime changes were reversed multiple times, creating investor uncertainty
Provincial development outside Lusaka and the Copperbelt received disproportionately less attention
improvementTips: Infrastructure development must be guided by a national spatial development plan with equitable provincial coverage
Mining fiscal policy should be stable and predictable to maintain investor confidence
Pro-poor policies require sustainable financing mechanisms to ensure long-term viability

scoreBreakdown.explanation: President Sata enjoyed strong public support, particularly among urban working-class Zambians who saw him as a champion of the common person. His landslide 2011 victory reflected deep public desire for change. His populist style, accessibility, and willingness to confront powerful interests earned him enduring loyalty, though trust was tested by media restrictions and governance concerns in his later presidency.
positiveFactors: Won the 2011 election with a clear majority, reflecting strong public mandate for change
Personally accessible and known for impromptu visits to markets, bus stations, and compounds
His populist rhetoric against exploitation by foreign mining companies resonated with ordinary Zambians
Infrastructure projects delivered visible improvements that citizens could see and appreciate
negativeFactors: Restrictions on The Post newspaper and selected media organizations raised press freedom concerns
Opacity around presidential health during his final year created public anxiety and rumour
Some supporters felt the pace of promised reform did not match campaign commitments
improvementTips: Transparency about presidential health is essential for public confidence and orderly governance
Protecting media freedom, even for critical outlets, strengthens democratic credibility
Managing public expectations through honest communication about reform timelines builds lasting trust

scoreBreakdown.explanation: While President Sata personally projected an anti-corruption image and made strong rhetorical commitments to fighting graft, his administration faced allegations of corruption involving officials close to him. The anti-corruption institutional framework was not significantly strengthened, and some procurement processes, particularly for road construction, were questioned for transparency.
positiveFactors: Strong anti-corruption rhetoric and public commitment to holding officials accountable
Personally modest lifestyle compared to predecessors, avoiding ostentatious displays of wealth
Initiated investigations into some Rupiah Banda-era corruption cases
negativeFactors: Several senior PF officials faced corruption allegations that were not pursued during his presidency
Road construction procurement under the Link Zambia 8000 programme lacked transparent competitive bidding in some cases
The Anti-Corruption Commission was not given additional resources or independence to match anti-corruption rhetoric
Allegations of political patronage in public service appointments, particularly at parastatal level
improvementTips: Anti-corruption commitments must be backed by institutional strengthening and adequate resourcing of oversight bodies
Large infrastructure procurement must follow transparent competitive processes with independent oversight
Public service appointments should be based on merit and managed through an independent commission

scoreBreakdown.explanation: President Sata managed Zambia's international relationships pragmatically, maintaining Chinese investment inflows while also engaging Western partners. His confrontational stance towards Chinese labour practices in Zambian mines attracted international attention but also created diplomatic tension. Zambia remained an active participant in SADC and AU affairs under his leadership.
positiveFactors: Maintained strong trade and investment relationships with China while demanding better labour standards
Continued Zambia's tradition of hosting refugees and contributing to regional stability
Advanced the Kazungula Bridge project, strengthening Zambia-Botswana economic integration
Engaged constructively in SADC political mediation processes
negativeFactors: Confrontational public rhetoric towards Chinese business practices created periodic diplomatic friction
Limited strategic engagement with emerging economies beyond China for investment diversification
Presidential health concerns reduced international engagement in the final year of his presidency
improvementTips: Diplomatic engagement with investment partners should balance firm policy positions with constructive dialogue
Investment attraction strategies should target a diverse range of source countries beyond traditional partners
Continuity in international engagement requires delegation to competent senior officials during presidential absence

overallExplanation: Michael Sata's truncated presidency (2011-2014) was characterized by decisive action, populist pro-poor policies, and rapid infrastructure delivery that resonated with ordinary Zambians. His creation of new administrative units, significant minimum wage increases, and transformation of Lusaka's road network represent lasting achievements. However, governance was marked by instability through frequent Cabinet changes, insufficient institutional strengthening of anti-corruption bodies, and opacity around presidential health. His untimely death in office in October 2014 cut short his reform agenda and left a complex legacy that blends genuine pro-poor commitment with governance shortcomings.
topImprovementAreas: Institutional strengthening of anti-corruption bodies must accompany anti-corruption rhetoric
Balanced provincial development ensures equitable growth beyond Lusaka and the Copperbelt
Presidential health transparency and succession planning are essential for governance continuity
